questions.question_text:
A distribution network has a unique minimum cut consisting of edges $SA$ and $SB$, with total capacity $35$.
Every other cut has capacity at least $40$. Edge $BC$ is not on the minimum cut.
Which upgrade increases maximum flow to $36$?

options.why: Leaves the minimum cut at $35$ because $BC$ is outside that cut.
Raises the minimum cut to $40$ rather than the required $36$; every other cut has capacity at least $40$.
Adds $2$ to the minimum cut, producing maximum flow $37$ rather than $36$.

questions.solution_text: Increase $SA$ by $1$. The minimum cut rises from $35$ to $36$, while every other cut has capacity at least $40$. The new maximum flow is $36$.

questions.question_text:
A network has minimum cut $C_1 = 50$ and second-smallest cut $C_2 = 56$.
An edge on $C_1$ is increased by $10$. Cut $C_2$ does not contain this edge.
What is the new maximum flow?

options.why: Assumed the flow increases by the full $10$ without checking that $C_2$ ($56$) becomes the new bottleneck.
Assumed the flow cannot change after an upgrade.
Added $10$ to cut $C_2$ instead of upgrading cut $C_1$.

questions.solution_text: New $C_1 = 50 + 10 = 60$. Cut $C_2$ stays at $56$ because it excludes the upgraded edge. Other cuts originally had capacity at least $56$ and cannot decrease after an upgrade. The new maximum flow is $56$.

questions.question_text:
An edge with capacity $30\text{ units}$ carries $18\text{ units}$ of flow in a maximum-flow assignment.
Its capacity is reduced to $22\text{ units}$.
What is the effect on the network's maximum flow?

options.text: Maximum flow is unchanged because the new capacity ($22$) still exceeds the utilised flow ($18$).

options.why: Subtracted the capacity reduction ($30 - 22 = 8$) directly from the maximum flow.
Subtracted the remaining slack ($22 - 18 = 4$) from maximum flow.
Assumed any capacity reduction halts all flow through the network.

questions.solution_text: The reduced capacity ($22$) still allows the edge flow ($18$) in the existing maximum-flow assignment. That assignment remains possible, and reducing capacity cannot increase maximum flow. Maximum flow is unchanged.

questions.question_text:
A pipeline network has a maximum flow of $180\text{ kL/day}$.
Demand is projected to reach $220\text{ kL/day}$.
The minimum cut consists of pipes $A$ and $B$, and all other cuts have capacity $\ge 240\text{ kL/day}$.
By how much must the capacity of pipe $A$ or $B$ be increased to meet demand?

options.why: Computed $240 - 180 = 60$ using an unrelated cut's capacity.
Confused the required increase with the total target demand.

questions.question_text:
The minimum cut of a road network has capacity $800\text{ vehicles/hour}$ across two roads ($500$ and $300$).
If both roads are widened by $100\text{ vehicles/hour}$ each and no other cut has capacity $< 1100$, what is the new maximum flow?

options.why: Added the upgrade for only one road ($800 + 100 = 900$) instead of both roads.
Took the next cut threshold instead of calculating the upgraded min cut capacity.
Assumed widening roads on the minimum cut has no effect.

questions.question_text:
In a network with maximum flow $75$, a bottleneck edge on the unique minimum cut has its capacity reduced by $15$.
What is the new maximum flow?

options.why: Assumed reducing a bottleneck edge has no effect on maximum flow.
Added the reduction ($75 + 15 = 90$) instead of subtracting it.
Confused the remaining maximum flow with the magnitude of the reduction.
